role.altitude: The genetic counselor keeps interviewing, interpreting, disclosing and explaining; copying histories and figures, drawing pedigrees from scratch and typing letters shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking scribe drafts and figure matches
role.ambitious_version: A counselor whose letter is ready the day of the consultation.

tasks.short: Have the patient fill in the family history questionnaire, interview the patient about family history, review records of the patient and relatives, request relatives' records, draw the pedigree, copy the history from the intake form into the record, document findings and discuss complex families with colleagues to obtain and document family medical histories.

steps.what: Patient fills in the family history questionnaire, on paper today and online before the visit after the change
Counselor interviews the patient to obtain a comprehensive family medical history
Counselor reviews medical records of the patient and consenting relatives
Counselor requests relatives' records from other hospitals by mail
Counselor draws the pedigree in the pedigree software from interview notes
Counselor copies the history from the paper intake form into the record
Counselor documents findings in the record

loop.input: The recorded intake conversation, with the patient's consent.
loop.output: A draft history note in the record's sections.
loop.check: A validator lists every statement about relatives, conditions or ages that cannot be found in the recorded intake; the counselor reads the draft against the interview, resolves each listed statement and corrects the rest before saving, and writes unclear parts by hand.
loop.stop: Intakes without consent are written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Family histories are told in free conversation.

steps.what: Counselor discusses complex families with colleagues

tasks.design: Patients fill in the family history online before the visit, which writes the record and pre-fills the pedigree with relatives, ages and conditions; the counselor corrects both during the interview. With consent, a certified scribe drafts the history note from the recorded intake and the counselor corrects it before saving. The interview, record review, record requests and colleague discussions stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Histories were copied from paper and pedigrees drawn from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Online family history forms feeding the record and pedigree, and certified scribes.
tasks.still_hard: Families with unknown or estranged relatives.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a family does not say.
tasks.altitude: Less copying and drawing; the interview stays.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts structured consultation notes into hospital record systems.
Genetic and health data are special category data.

assumptions: Boundary: obtaining and documenting histories; writing consultation reports (task 17511 in this set) is a separate task with its own letter.

Input contract: about 70% of patients complete the online questionnaire; s5 keeps 50 for corrections and s6 keeps 35 for the paper forms that remain and checking what the form wrote. The patient's form time is shown in s1.
s7 keeps 70 because every draft is corrected; this is an estimate with no measured case in the digest.
The means prior puts 52% in person; the steps show 47%, because records, requests, pedigree and notes take 52%.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients fill the form online and many decline recording, so s5 keeps 90, s6 keeps 80 and s7 keeps 100 (2.8); high: about 70% online and most consent (15.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain inheritance patterns and risks in the session, talk with family members who join, draw diagrams, give approved leaflets, look up current risk figures, let patients ask the answer desk and answer follow-up questions by phone and mail to provide information about the inheritance of conditions.

steps.what: Counselor provides information about the inheritance of conditions in the session
Counselor talks with family members who join the session
Counselor draws inheritance diagrams for the patient
Counselor selects and gives approved leaflets
Counselor looks up current risk figures in guidelines
Patient asks the answer desk follow-up questions about the leaflets
Counselor answers follow-up questions by phone and mail

loop.input: The patient's general question and the approved patient leaflets.
loop.output: An answer quoting the leaflet paragraph, marked as AI.
loop.check: Every reply is a word-for-word passage from an approved leaflet with the leaflet named; a question that matches no passage clearly, or mentions the patient's own risk, results or family, goes to the counselor; the counselor reads a weekly sample to check the passages answered the questions asked.
loop.stop: Questions about the patient's own risk or results go to the counselor.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients ask in their own words.

tasks.design: An answer desk on the approved leaflets shows the patient the passages that match a general follow-up question, word for word with the leaflet named and marked as automatic, and writes no text of its own; anything about the patient's own risk or results, or without a clear match, goes to the counselor. Sessions, family talks, diagrams, leaflets and risk figures stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every general follow-up question came to the counselor.
tasks.enabler_now: An answer desk over approved leaflets.
tasks.still_hard: Anxious patients who need a person.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining a 25% risk so a family can live with it.

evidence.claim: Patient-facing chat must say it is AI.
An answer desk can answer from approved leaflets and quote its source.

assumptions: Boundary: providing inheritance information; preparing educational materials (task 17518) is a sibling task.
s7 keeps 75: about a quarter of follow-up questions are general ones the leaflets answer; the patient's time is shown in s6.
The means prior puts 59% in person; the steps show 67%, because the session is the core of the task.
research_questions: Do fewer general questions reach the counselor?

incremental.description: Counselor reads a weekly sample of answer desk replies.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients use the desk, so s7 keeps 90 (0.9); high: about a quarter of follow-up questions answered by leaflet passages (2.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the lab report and variant classification, look up the variant in databases and literature, discuss the result with the clinical geneticist, phone the patient, disclose results in person, inform the referring physician, copy variant details into the record and note the disclosure to interpret laboratory results and communicate findings.

steps.what: Counselor interprets the laboratory report and variant classification
Counselor looks up the variant in databases and literature
Counselor discusses the result with the clinical geneticist
Counselor phones the patient to arrange the result talk
Counselor communicates findings to the patient in person
Counselor informs the referring physician
Counselor copies variant name and classification from the lab report into the record
Counselor notes the disclosure in the record

tasks.design: Lab results arrive as structured messages that write the variant name and classification into the record, instead of the counselor copying them. Interpreting, research, the geneticist talk, calls, disclosure, informing the physician and the disclosure note stay with the counselor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Variant details were copied from PDF reports.
tasks.human_edge: Telling a family hard news well.

evidence.claim: Labs can send structured result messages that write variant fields into the record.
Genetic and health data are special category data.

assumptions: Boundary: interpreting and communicating results; analyzing genetic information for risk (task 17500) is a sibling task.
s6 is part of writing detailed consultation reports, which task 17511 in this set covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s7: about 80% of results come from labs that send structured messages; s7 is priced at that share and keeps 20.
The means prior puts 51% in person; the steps show 42%, because reading the report, research and the record take 40%.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of results come as structured messages, so s7 keeps 60 (2.0); high: about 80% structured as assumed (4.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write the consultation letter, copy variant details and risk figures from the lab report and risk tools into it, write plain-language explanations, insert the pedigree, discuss the draft with the clinical geneticist, check and sign it, send it, answer questions about it and file a copy to write detailed consultation reports for patients or referring physicians.

steps.what: Counselor writes the detailed consultation report

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with consent, and the saved record.
loop.output: A draft letter in the clinic's sections.
loop.check: A validator lists every statement not found in the consultation recording, and variant names and risk figures must match the lab report or sending is blocked; the counselor reads each section against the consultation, resolves each listed statement and rewrites what does not match.
loop.stop: Consultations without consent are written by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each family's situation is explained in its own words.

steps.what: Counselor copies variant details and risk figures from the lab report and risk tools into the letter
Counselor writes plain-language explanations of complex genetic concepts
Counselor exports the pedigree image and inserts it into the letter
Counselor discusses the draft with the clinical geneticist
Counselor checks the final letter: content against the consultation, variant and figures against the lab report, and the patient and physician it goes to, and signs it
Counselor sends the signed letter to the patient and referring physician
Counselor answers questions about the letter
Counselor files a copy of the letter in the record

approvals.approved_version: The consultation letter exactly as checked and signed by the counselor in s6, with variant names and risk figures matching the lab report, sent once to the named patient and physician; any change needs a new signature.

tasks.design: With consent, a certified scribe drafts the letter from the recorded consultation; the counselor rewrites and corrects every section. A letter template fills variant names, classifications and risk figures from the structured lab result and risk tool, and inserts the pedigree; any mismatch with the lab report blocks sending. Plain-language explanations, the geneticist discussion, signing, sending and questions stay with the counselor; the signed letter files itself to the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Letters were typed after each consultation and figures copied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified scribes and letter templates fed by lab results.
tasks.still_hard: Families with several conditions in one letter.
tasks.human_edge: Writing risk so a family understands it.
tasks.altitude: Less typing and copying; explanation stays.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber drafts structured consultation notes into hospital record systems.
Software giving information used for diagnostic or therapeutic decisions is MDR class IIa or higher.
Genetic and health data are special category data.

assumptions: Boundary: writing consultation reports; this task carries the letter-writing saving for the other tasks in this set.
s1 keeps 70 because every section is rewritten and checked; no measured case for genetics letters is in the digest, so this is an estimate.
s2 keeps 30 for checking figures and copying them from results that still arrive as PDF; s4 and s9 keep 30.
The means prior puts 38% on documents; the steps show 63%, because writing the letter dominates.
research_questions: Do letters reach physicians sooner without figure errors?

incremental.description: Counselor joins a monthly sample audit of drafts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients decline recording and more results arrive as PDF, so s1 keeps 100 and s2 keeps 50 (10.1); high: most consent and about 80% structured results (21.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
